title: What does XLS-47 specify for Price oracles?
abstract: Sourced explanation of XLS-47 and its practical limits.
body:
According to XLS specifications, XLS-47 specifies price-oracle entries for publishing asset-price data on XRPL. [1]

An oracle publisher records data for specified asset pairs and update times. Ledger inclusion makes the publication inspectable but does not independently verify the market price. Consumers still choose acceptable sources and freshness limits. A published quote is distinct from an executable offer, so it does not promise that a buyer can trade the quoted amount at that price. [1]

The public XLS-47 specification describes a design, its dependencies and its intended ledger behavior. A published standard is not proof that a feature is enabled on every XRPL network. Check the target network and any associated fixes before relying on the capability. Testnet, Mainnet and development networks can support different amendment sets, and examples in a proposal are explanatory rather than records of validated transactions. [1][2]

The fetched specification records its status as Final. [1] Author interpretation: compare the proposed use of XLS-47 with the actual network capability and preserve the resulting evidence. Keep a design reference separate from a deployment claim and from a successful transaction receipt. This article makes no fresh network-activation claim. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
